rubric_feedback: Q7(d): the answer correctly locates the zero rule in memorandum sec. 1(a)(ii) (91 FR 47720) but also wrongly in the 'last two sentences' of note 52(k). I checked note 52(k) at 91 FR 47394: those two sentences state only the below-cap sum rule, so the key is right and the answer is partly wrong; because q7d_zero's 'no if' disqualifier is triggered I graded it no, though a grader might read the criterion as satisfied since the memorandum is named. Q13: the key's (e) turns on Commerce guidance FR Doc. 2026-20938 (91 FR 65162), which I verified exists (published 14 Oct. 2026, effective for entries on/after that date); the submission missed it entirely, giving $45,000 for both (e) and (f), so q13e is no while q13f is yes — the rubric's split works. Q14 item 5: the submission's narrow claim that only the EU, Switzerland and Taiwan have economy-specific 'Parts' is factually wrong (thirteen economies have particular-article lists in note 52(j) at 91 FR 47365-47394, verified by grep), which the criterion already captures. Q11: of the submission's ten items only five are valid; several are on the key's do-not-count list (the TRQ 'September 1' recital, the in-transit silence, the 'suspension' framing) and items 1 and 3 are the same discrepancy (11056 chapeau-only amendment) counted twice.
